title: We checked 9.7 million posts about what people think about AI on the day before the Anthropic IPO. Reddit has turned against the AI trade.
author: rumor_io
selftext:
We searched 1.7 billion posts we hold on Reddit, StockTwits, YouTube and X for posts about AI, then had a language model read a sample of about 80,000 posts and write down what each author believes. 

The short version: **people stopped arguing about whether AI works. They now argue about who pays for it.**

Of the 9.7 million posts, about four in ten matches are not really about AI (a passing mention, "ask ChatGPT", a bot signature, a crypto coin with "AI" in its name). The language model marked those and they are left out of our analysis.

# The five findings

* **Reddit has turned against the AI trade.** Among Reddit posts that take a side, skeptics passed believers in the last quarter. In 2023 and 2024 believers led about three to one.
* **StockTwits stayed bullish for three years and cracked this month.** Believers led about four to one until October. In the week of 16 November skeptics led for the first time.
* **Belief in the technology did not fall.** The share of people calling AI overhyped went down, not up. What grew is doubt about the money: "the labs will never earn it back", "the companies are paying each other", "it is built on debt".
* **OpenAI is disliked everywhere. Anthropic was liked until its numbers came out.** Through 2025 about four in five opinions about Anthropic were positive. In 2026, with the listing papers public, more than half are negative on Reddit and YouTube.
* **Almost nobody on Reddit says "I will buy on day one".** The betting market disagrees with them: it gives about a 90% chance that the shares close above the listing price on the first day.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the shift from "does it work" to "who pays for it" matches what I see in trading threads too, nobody argues the models are useless anymore, they argue about capex. did the skeptic share move before NVDA did or after it?

replies.author: rumor_io
replies.body: Hey u/QuanTradin! I just posted our latest chart above. You see a fall over the past two months along with the NVDA price for sure, but I think it's part of the steady decline in belief since June.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: a steady slide since June reads more like belief wearing out than people reacting to the price. if it were price-driven it would jump around with every NVDA swing, and a smooth line like yours doesn't do that.
